correctness.rationale: The Finding's ordinary-node and rationality statements are correct, but the unqualified title 'Eleven split isolated nodes' is false under the standard tangent-cone meaning of split over the residue field. At a sign point x, put P=∏x_i. On ∑u_i=0 the Hessian form is 2P∑x_i u_i², by expanding the torus factor ∑X_i⁻¹. The projective radical is the radial line. In the chart u5=0, u4=−∑_{i=0}^3u_i, the rank-four Hessian matrix is 2P times a diagonal sign matrix plus x4 times the all-ones matrix (inside the same scalar). Its determinant is (2P)^4(∏_{i=0}^3 x_i)(1+x4∑_{i=0}^3 x_i)=−P. Thus the ten balanced nodes have square determinant, whereas E has determinant 2, nonsquare, and is nonsplit over F3. All are nonetheless rational and ordinary. Independently, on the boundary at most three nonzero coordinates give the twenty lines, exactly four nonzero coordinates give unequal derivatives, and exactly five are impossible. On the torus equal partials force equal squares and the hyperplane leaves precisely the six-equal and balanced sign points up to negation. Supports 2,3,4,6 contribute 15,20,45,11 rational points respectively; support four is smooth, since the two gradient values differ, and its 45 points are C(6,4)C(4,2)/2. This gives 46 singular and 91 total, retested with `python3 /workspace/audit-work/finite_checks.py`. No scheme thickening along the lines is checked.

Sum with 46 to get 91. Likewise the already recorded rank-four determinants 2 and 1 yield nonsplit and split respectively by the determinant square-class criterion over F3. A corrected title would not leave a distinct arithmetic result.
